title: Burst-aware rolling batcher with KV snapshotting and memory reclamation
creator: Ava Chen
description: Problem statement: Mixed prompt/response workloads produce bursts of short, chatty turns interleaved with long generation requests. Existing continuous batcher strategies either keep KV residency aggressively (causing GPU memory pressure) or evict too eagerly (causing expensive KV rebuilds during bursts). This ticket implements a burst-aware rolling batching layer that coordinates: 1) short-window burst detection, 2) incremental KV snapshotting to enable fast rehydration of recently used KV slices, and 3) opportunistic memory reclamation (GPU slab compaction + async eviction) to reduce tail memory fragmentation during steady-state long generations. Goals: reduce out-of-memory incidents on 80GB GPUs under mixed traffic, lower p95 latency for bursty short-turns, and limit extra token-cost from rebuilding KV caches. Deliverables: code changes in continuous-batcher, a KV snapshot/restore library, bench harness, perf dashboards, and rollback/feature-flag gating for runtime rollout.
acceptance_criteria: New rolling-batcher component is feature-flagged behind runtime flag 'burst_rolling_v1'
Under combined synthetic workload (50% short-turns <16 tokens, 50% long-gen average 1024 tokens) p95 latency of short-turns improves by >= 15% vs baseline with same token throughput
GPU memory fragmentation metric (per-GPU free-slab ratio) improves by >= 20% during mixed workloads compared to baseline
KV rehydration time measured from snapshot is < 12ms for 90% of hot slices
No increase in token-cost per request > 3% on average across bench suite
Automated e2e perf job added to CI (bench: mixed-dialogue-burst) that fails if p99 latency regresses > 10%
Design doc and migration guide published, and early canary rollout executed in 2 clusters with rollback plan validated
technical_notes: Burst detector: sliding time window (200ms) with adaptive threshold on short-turn ratio and arriving qps spike detection

KV snapshot: incremental per-slab snapshot with LRU timestamp metadata; snapshots persisted in host memory and optionally NVMe cache for rapid restore; serialized format reuses existing KV layout to avoid extra copy
Memory reclamation: async compaction thread that coalesces free slabs and triggers deferred evictions only when free-slab ratio below watermark; integrates with existing KV eviction callbacks

Batching policy: rolling window groups prioritized by 'burst_hot' tag; during burst mode allow smaller window coalescing with tight latency cap; outside burst, favor larger windows to maximize throughput
Failure modes: snapshot write/restore errors degrade to existing full-rebuild path; must be observable and auto-fail to safe behavior
Compatibility: backward-compatible with current KV format; feature gated; supports mixed-precision + quantized kernels
Telemetry: new metrics - burst_mode_active, snapshot_write_ms, snapshot_restore_ms, reclamation_compactions, free_slab_ratio, kv_rebuild_count
Bench harness: uses mixed-dialogue-simulator with configurable burstiness, token-length distribution and QPS shaping; results uploaded to perf dashboards for regression tracking
steps: 1) Prototype burst detector and integrate into continuous-batcher control loop
2) Implement incremental per-slab KV snapshot & in-memory index
3) Add async memory reclamation thread and slab compaction APIs
4) Wire feature flagging and runtime config knobs (thresholds, snapshot TTL, reclamation interval)
5) Add comprehensive unit tests + integration test that simulates host memory and GPU OOM scenarios
6) Run microbench and e2e bench suite, tune thresholds based on observations
7) Prepare design doc, migration plan, and run canary rollout with close telemetry review
8) Promote to staged rollout and monitor for one week before broad release
qa_plan: Unit tests for snapshot/restore correctness and edge cases (partial snapshot, concurrent writes)
Integration tests for rolling-batcher under synthetic burst traffic at multiple QPS levels
Stress test: extended mixed workload for 72 hours to validate memory stability and fragmentation metrics
Canary gating: deploy to 2 small clusters, run smoke + perf checks for 48 hours, validate no OOMs and acceptable latency
Run CI e2e perf job and ensure metrics uploaded to dashboard; require sign-off from perf eng
rollout_plan: Alpha: internal build with feature flag enabled for dev clusters only
Canary: enable 'burst_rolling_v1' for 5% of production traffic in two non-critical regions; monitor free_slab_ratio and p95 latency
Gradual ramp: increase to 25% over 72 hours if metrics stable, then 65% over 5 days
Full: enable by default for runtime-1.22 after 7-day stability window
Rollback: flip feature flag off and run KV rebuild job to return to previous eviction/residency behavior; rollback playbook documented
updates: 2025-11-14 - Ava Chen: Spike completed. Prototype burst detector integrated into local cluster; initial thresholds (200ms window, 3x baseline short-turn ratio) chosen from replay traces. Observed immediate p95 short-turn improvement in dev harness.

2025-11-21 - Miguel Torres: Implemented slab-level KV snapshot and basic restore. Snapshot serialize/deserialize works end-to-end but restore latency spikes on cold NVMe; investigating in-memory caching of hot-slices.

2025-11-26 - Miguel Torres: Added async reclamation thread. Early runs show free_slab_ratio improvement but introduced small CPU contention; moved compaction to lower-priority worker and limited run-frequency to 500ms.

2025-11-28 - QA: Added integration scenarios to bench harness to simulate back-to-back bursts. Recorded baseline vs feature-flagged runs; preparing dashboard tiles for snapshot_restore_ms and kv_rebuild_count.

2025-12-03 - Miguel Torres: Canary checklist drafted. Need PM sign-off on rollout windows and perf guardrails. Next: finalize cleanup edge-case handling and add automated rollback verifier for snapshot integrity.
